title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday a student tells the makerspace assistant their preferred booking time. On Wednesday they start a new session and the assistant does not know it. What explains this?

options.text: The context window was too small to hold Monday's chat
The model forgot it because its weights are updated slowly
Nothing carried over unless the program saved it and reloaded it
The model ignored the fact because it sat mid-conversation

items.stem: An agent starts with 1,000 tokens (system prompt, tools, question). Each step adds 500 tokens (the model's request plus the tool result). It makes 3 model calls. Every call receives the full context so far. How many input tokens are read in total across the 3 calls?
The assistant must answer from a 60-page manual of about 36,000 tokens, across 5 model calls per request, on a small budget. Which design is best?

options.text: Search the manual and add only the few best-matching chunks
Load the whole manual because the window is big enough
Save the whole manual as a note for the model to recall
Ask the model to memorize the manual during the session

items.stem: Give one reason, in one sentence, why putting an entire long document in the context can give worse answers than putting in only the relevant part, apart from cost.
A long run is nearing the limit. Early tool results are no longer needed, but the student's confirmed machine certification must still be known next week. What is the best handling?

options.text: Clear the old results and save the certification as a note
Keep every result in the context so nothing is lost
Clear the old results and trust the summary to survive
Restart the conversation and have the student repeat it
